correctness.rationale: At every ideal cusp the cross-section is bounded Euclidean polygon Q and distance to incident vertical planes is asinh(horizontal distance/z). The inner planar erosion has area loss L t - C(Q)t² with C(Q)=∑cot(theta/2) until first combinatorial event. Integrating z^-3 over z0≤z≤η/sinh s gives (L/z0)s - C(Q)s² log(1/s)+O(s²). Higher cusp tail and compact face/edge seam terms contribute only O(s²). Each ideal 3D edge appears in two vertex figures, giving B(P)=2∑_e cot(beta_e/2). Ideal face area and Euler supply total boundary area 2π(v-2). For tetrahedra strict Jensen gives B≥12√3 and standard Lobachevsky formula gives maximal volume v3 only at regular, yielding the normalized bound. Source checker uses independent half-plane erosion and cusp integration on triangular and square sections, corroborative not a proof of the general limit.
